It is reached via an 80-meter-deep, two-lane road right-of-way (pending an easement negotiation with the neighboring owner) that connects to a 20-meter-wide public street; this right-of-way drains west at a gentle 1/3-of-1% grade and is bordered by 2.4-meter sidewalks on each side, with the sidewalk surface set as the 0.0-meter benchmark elevation. The building site itself slopes uniformly at 8%, both toward the right-of-way and toward a vacant lot at the front. An empty parcel lies to the site's left as seen from the right-of-way, while three-storey single-family homes back onto the rear boundary. The brief calls for a building that (1) appeals to middle-income tenants, (2) maximizes the developer's rental income through a 70:30 saleable-to-non-saleable split of the leasable area, itself 85% of the total gross floor area, and (3) reads as a cost-efficient neighborhood landmark.

q: Which of these could be the side dimension of a square bedside table?
n: A typical bedside table side dimension is around 400mm — the other values are either far too small to be functional or far larger than a nightstand would ever be. — per the source document.

n: When a chair must be pulled back and a person also needs to pass behind it, roughly 950mm of clearance from the table edge to the wall is required. — per the source document.

q: Among these, which item does NOT count as a furnishing?
n: A freestanding wardrobe cabinet (armoire) is a piece of furniture rather than a furnishing. Paintings, decorative rugs, and even an ornamental ceiling fan are typically treated as furnishings/décor. — per the source document.

q: What length would be plausible for a three-seat sofa?
n: A three-seat sofa typically runs about 1,800mm in length; 600mm, 900mm, or 1,200mm would be too short to seat three people. — per the source document.

o: As close as possible to the largest, most expensive units
